title: Potential-force commutator obstruction for the resolvent-smoothed coordinate
question: Does the potential-force term V'(q) f'(q) in the second Heisenberg commutator remain uniformly K-form bounded for the fixed resolvent-smoothed coordinate f(q)=16q/(16+q^2)?
method: Use y=q^2 and the exact Q3 shifted potential V=17/12-y/2+3y^2/20, force V'=q(-1+3y/5), and resolvent derivative |f'|=16(y-16)/(16+y)^2 on y>=64.
Prove the exact lower bounds |V'|/|q|>=y/2, |f'|>=2/y, and V>=y^2/20, so |V'f'|>=|q| and V|V'f'|^2>=y^3/20.

Interpret the pointwise inequality on translated compactly supported C1 bumps with finite derivative energy C_phi: the potential part of the numerator grows like R^6 while the K-form denominator grows like R^4, giving a route-local unbounded ratio.
Reproduce the rational y-grid independently and compile Lean R308 for the force, derivative, combined numerator and potential polynomial inequalities.
finding: Primary 50/50, independent 36/36, integrated 12/12, and Lean R308 PASS. On y=q^2>=64 the exact force/derivative lower bounds give |V'(q)f'(q)|>=|q|, while the shifted potential satisfies V(q)>=q^4/20. Hence the potential contribution V|V'f'|^2 is at least q^6/20. Under the declared translated compact-support C1 localization test with finite derivative energy C_phi, the corresponding weighted numerator/denominator ratio grows at least like q^2. This obstructs the naive K-form multiplication route for the potential-force component of a second commutator, even at fixed resolvent scale.
decision_reason: This is a route-local coercive obstruction rather than a finite numerical miss. Resolvent smoothing controls f and its first derivative, but the Q3 quartic force leaves a linear tail in V'f'. The result blocks only the naive second-commutator K-form route; cancellation-aware combinations, higher-energy/state-weighted norms, modular estimates, and different carriers remain open.
